players.comment: Slovis (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Panthers but will serve as the Ravens' emergency quarterback. Slovis will be inactive once again. However, if Jacoby Brissett and Joe Fagnano exit Sunday's meeting with Carolina due to an injury, illness or ejection, Slovis will be available to play.

Johnson played all 17 of his snaps on special teams and recorded one tackle in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Bears. Johnson, a reserve wide receiver, has been used almost exclusively on special teams through his two-plus seasons in Tampa Bay. He's logged just 15 total snaps on offense through nine games in 2026, recording a three-yard reception on two targets. Johnson leads the Buccaneers with 14 kickoff returns for 389 yards, but he didn't see any runback opportunities in Week 9 while Sean Tucker handled those duties.

Yankoff (knee) was a full participant at practice Thursday. Yankoff sat out the Commanders' contest against the Giants in Week 10 because of a knee injury, but it now looks like he's put it behind him. He figures to resume a depth role at tight end in Week 11 against the Bengals.

The Broncos elevated Schrader from their practice squad to their active roster Saturday, Susanna Weir of the team's official site reports. Schrader's elevation is his third of the season, so he'll need to be signed to Denver's active roster in order to see game action for the team beyond Sunday. In his previous two appearances, the third-year pro played a total of two offensive snaps and nine snaps on special teams without recording any carries or targets. Schrader isn't likely to be much of a factor on offense Sunday against Las Vegas, as Jonah Coleman and J.K. Dobbins should continue to lead the Broncos' backfield. However, Schrader could contribute as a kick returner -- he's tallied 68 yards on three kickoff returns this season.

Jones (shoulder) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the 49ers in Mexico City. Jones -- who was managing a shoulder injury during Week 11 prep -- was a full participant in Friday's session, which was enough for him to avoid an injury tag for Sunday's contest. He was signed to the Vikings' 53-man roster Wednesday to give the team more depth at wide receiver while Jordan Addison recovers from a thumb injury. Jones figures to be limited to a rotational role on offense while serving as a contributor on special teams.

The Vikings placed Richter (foot) on injured reserve Wednesday. Richter will now be forced to miss at least four games after suffering a foot injury during the Week 10 win over the Packers. The 26-year-old has compiled six tackles (three solo) across nine appearances this season while playing almost exclusively on special teams.

Wilson (hand/finger) is active for Sunday's game against the Eagles. The third-year wideout was activated from injured reserve Saturday, foreshadowing his availability for Sunday's contest following a four-game absence. Wilson recorded at least three receptions in his first four games of the season on his way to a 14-188-2 line on 25 targets, and he then failed to reel in the only pass thrown his way in Week 5 against the Colts before exiting that game at halftime with his injury. In his return Sunday against Philadelphia, Wilson should slot into the No. 3 receiver role behind DK Metcalf and rookie Germie Bernard, the latter who leapfrogged Wilson on the depth chart over the last several games while filling in for both him and Michael Pittman (IR, foot).

Wilson recorded 19 tackles (nine solo) in Sunday's 38-18 loss to the Bengals. Wilson not only set a career high with his 19 stops, he also tied the NFL high mark by any player so far this season. The third-year linebacker has jumped up a notch as an IDP asset in 2026, as he's tied for sixth in the league with 88 stops through nine games. Wilson has also added a sack, three defensed passes (including one interception) and a fumble recovery.

Shipley (foot) is active for Sunday's game against Pittsburgh. Shipley was activated from injured reserve Saturday, and the third-year running back has been officially cleared to return from a four-game absence due to a partial plantar fascia tear that he sustained in Week 5 against the Jaguars. Shipley and Jaydon Blue will operate as the Eagles' rotational running backs behind Saquon Barkley for Sunday's game against a Steelers defense that ranks third in the NFL in rushing yards allowed per game (83.2).

Barner caught all three targets for 19 yards in Sunday's 21-13 win over the Raiders. Barner has been held below 25 receiving yards in eight of 10 games this season and has more rushing touchdowns (two) than receiving scores (one) during the 2026 campaign. He's the definition of a low-floor, touchdown-or-bust fantasy option headed into the team's bye week.

Allen rushed eight times for 40 yards and caught his only target for six yards in Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills. For a second consecutive game, Allen was outplayed by Breece Hall, who produced 108 scrimmage yards on 15 touches. Allen remains the more efficient runner, averaging 5.0 yards per carry to Hall's 3.4 this season, but Hall is the team's preferred option in passing situations, which have been plentiful with the 2-8 Jets frequently in catch-up mode. Perhaps a Week 11 matchup with a Chargers team that's still searching for its first win through Sunday of Week 10 will offer an opportunity to stick with the run and play to Allen's strengths.

Ali played all 19 of his snaps on special teams in Monday's 23-20 loss to the Chargers. For the second week in a row, Ali was deployed exclusively on special teams while the Ravens leaned on Derrick Henry and Justice Hill to handle all the snaps out of the backfield. Ali has logged just seven total snaps on offense all season, carrying six times for 24 yards.

Davis didn't touch the ball on offense in Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills. With Breece Hall and Braelon Allen both healthy, Davis has minimal fantasy value, except for leagues that count return yardage. He's played zero offensive snaps over the last two contests, but Davis did return three kickoffs for 74 yards against Buffalo.

Lloyd finished Sunday's loss to Minnesota with 13 yards on four carries while catching all three of his targets for 26 yards. With Josh Jacobs (finger) sidelined, Green Bay turned to the trio of Lloyd, Kaleb Johnson and Chris Brooks in the backfield. Johnson led the team with 10 carries and 42 total yards despite not getting any targets. Meanwhile, Lloyd turned his seven touches into 39 yards, and Brooks tallied just three yards on his three touches. Green Bay is on bye during the coming week, but Jacobs may still miss the team's next game, which will take place Wednesday, Nov. 25, against the Rams. If that's the case, Lloyd will likely work as part of a shared backfield again, which isn't great for his fantasy outlook.

Williams logged eight tackles (two solo) and a pass defense during the Packers' 30-10 loss to the Vikings in Week 10. Williams played every single defensive snap in Week 10 and finished tied for the second-most tackles on the Packers behind Isaiah McDuffie (10). Williams has recorded at least eight stops in three of his last four outings and is up to 84 tackles (50 solo), including 1.0 sacks, eight pass defenses (including three interceptions) and a fumble recovery through 10 regular-season games. He is well on track to surpass 100 tackles for a second consecutive year.

Gould secured two of three targets for 48 yards in the Colts' 26-3 loss to the Texans on Thursday. Gould was the rather unlikely leader in receiving yards for the Colts on the night, with a team-high 31-yard catch playing a big role in getting him there. The 2024 fifth-round pick has seen an expanded role in the wake of the trades of Josh Downs and Keenan Allen, and for as long as Alec Pierce (IR, heel) is sidelined, Gould could function as one of Indianapolis' top downfield threats for either Daniel Jones, Anthony Richardson or Riley Leonard.

The Chiefs placed Wiley (ankle) on injured reserve Wednesday, Matt Derrick of ChiefsDigest.com reports. Wiley was carted to the locker room in the first quarter of the Chiefs' Week 10 win over the Falcons with an ankle injury. The tight end will now be on IR as he nurses his fractured ankle until at least the latter part of the regular season. Travis Kelce, Noah Gray and Jake Briningstool are now the only tight ends on the Chiefs' active roster.

Trotter recorded 11 tackles (five solo) and one forced fumble during the Eagles' 19-11 loss to the Giants in Week 9. Trotter was on the field for 64 of the Eagles' 67 defensive snaps (95.5 percent), and he was the only Philadelphia defender to reach double-digit stops. He's tallied at least 10 tackles three times in 2026, and the third-year pro is up to 51 tackles (32 solo), including 0.5 sacks, one pass defense and one forced fumble through nine regular-season games.

Eboigbe (ankle) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Jets. Eboigbe was unable to play against the Ravens this past Monday due to an ankle injury. He ended Week 11 prep with a full practice Friday, which was enough for him to avoid an injury tag ahead of Sunday's contest. His return means there will be less rotational snaps at defensive end for rookie fifth-rounder Nick Barrett.

Smith recorded seven tackles (four solo) and an interception in Sunday night's 27-24 loss to the Bears. As a team, the Bucs picked off Caleb Williams four times Sunday night, but it still wasn't enough to propel Tampa Bay to a win. Smith now has two picks over his last three games and is up to 50 tackles (26 solo), three pass breakups and a forced fumble across nine starts this season. He has a chance to best last season's career-high 100 tackles in 2026.

Johnson logged one catch (on three targets) for eight yards Thursday in a loss to the Commanders. Johnson hasn't been able to get going in 2026, as he's finished with one or zero catches in six of his seven games so far. After working as New York's top tight end last season, he's been mostly an afterthought in the current campaign due to the arrival of Isaiah Likely, who went off for a 9-127-1 line on a team-leading 11 targets Thursday. As long as Likely is healthy, Johnson won't have much appeal in most fantasy formats.
inactive inactive

Maye, who sustained a fractured right fibula in last Sunday's loss to the Lions, is on track to miss at least six weeks, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports. The timetable put forth by Rapoport suggests that Maye could make a run at a late-season return, or for the postseason, should New England qualify. Given that the Patriots are already close to the limit of how many players they can designate for return from injured reserve, Maye isn't a lock to land on IR, but he's nonetheless facing an absence longer than the required four games that a placement on IR would mandate. For now, Tommy DeVito has been installed as the team's starter ahead of its Week 12 matchup against the Chargers, with rookie Behren Morton on hand as his backup.

Head coach Todd Bowles suggested Monday that McMillan (knee) isn't likely to immediately return to action following the Buccaneers' Week 10 bye, Rick Stroud of the Tampa Bay Times reports. While Bowles indicated that linebacker Yaya Diaby (knee) has decent odds of playing in the Buccaneers' next game Nov. 22 versus the Lions, the coach was less optimistic about McMillan's chances of being ready to play in Week 11. The Buccaneers have yet to open McMillan's 21-day practice window, after he was placed on injured reserve Sept. 30 due to a PCL sprain in his left knee, which was an aggravation of a previous injury. Bowles noted that McMillan underwent a medical procedure on the knee shortly after landing on IR and is still dealing with some discomfort.

Gray posted nine tackles (eight solo) and two pass defenses (including an interception) during the Titans' 40-23 loss to the Jaguars in Week 10. Gray was cleared to return from a one-game absence due to a concussion. The third-year linebacker led the Titans in both total and solo tackles, and he also picked off a pass from Trevor Lawrence intended for Jakobi Meyers midway through the first quarter, although Tennessee's offense was not able to convert that takeaway into points. Gray is up to 46 tackles (26 solo), including 0.5 sacks, and two pass defenses (one interception) through eight regular-season games.

Rakestraw (shoulder) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Buccaneers. A shoulder injury limited Rakestraw's practice reps during Week 11 prep. He was initially tagged as questionable, but after he went through pregame warmups, medical staff has determined that Rakestraw is not in good enough shape to suit up for Sunday's contest. With D.J. Reed (hip) also sidelined, Khalil Dorsey figures to start opposite Rock Ya-Sin at outside cornerback. Rakestraw's next opportunity to play is Thanksgiving Day against the Bears.

Franklin brought in three of four targets for 31 yards during the Broncos' 26-21 win over the Panthers on Sunday. Franklin drew a 27-yard pass interference penalty on the Broncos' second offensive play of the game, but the third-year wide receiver didn't log his first catch until early in the fourth quarter. He has operated in a rotational role for most of the season, and even with Jaylen Waddle in the league's concussion protocol, Franklin will likely maintain that workload following the Broncos' Week 10 bye.

Bishop (knee) was a full participant in practice Thursday, Sal Capaccio of WGR Sports Radio 550 Buffalo reports. The safety was limited during Wednesday's session. Bishop has yet to miss a game this season, and it doesn't appear that streak will be snapped Sunday. He has 54 tackles (32 solo), including 1.0 sacks, two pass breakups and a forced fumble in 2026.

Davis (hamstring) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Dolphins. The backup running back was managed during the practice week but is good to go for his normal role behind lead back James Cook. With the Bills listed as 16.5-point favorites, Davis could see some extra reps in garbage time if Buffalo does indeed blow out Miami.

With Omar Cooper (ankle) ruled out, Mitchell is expected to play an elevated role on offense Sunday against the Chargers. Cooper was injured early in last Sunday's loss to the Bills, and Mitchell went on to see eight targets, as the Jets were playing catch-up most of the afternoon. They might be able to keep things closer against the 1-8 Chargers, though Los Angeles is still favored in the contest. Mitchell is a big-play threat as a WR4 for fantasy purposes.

Thomas caught three of four targets for 29 yards in Sunday's 40-23 win over the Titans. The three catches tied his season high, while the four targets represented his biggest volume since Week 2. The Jaguars' decision not to deal Thomas at the trade deadline remains a curious one, as the third-year wideout simply doesn't have a significant role in Liam Coen's offense and might not step into one even if someone like Parker Washington got injured -- Josh Cameron was more productive Sunday on three targets and caught one of Trevor Lawrence's three TDs. Thomas will take a 13-146-2 line on 26 targets over nine games into a Week 11 tilt against the Giants.

Worthy failed to catch any of his three targets in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Falcons. Worthy ran a team-high 37 routes on Patrick Mahomes' 38 dropbacks, but on a day Mahomes targeted nine different players, Worthy was the only one to not record a catch. With Josh Downs now in the fold and working to get comfortable in the offense, Worthy's role will likely only continue to shrink. On just eight routes in his team debut Sunday, Downs posted a 4-53-1 receiving line on five targets. Worthy hasn't produced that many fantasy points in a game all season. He's waiver-wire fodder in 12-team redraft leagues.

Coleman caught one of three targets for 11 yards during Sunday's 31-12 win over the Jets. Coleman failed to reel in multiple passes for the third time in the team's last five contests, and he played just 52 percent of the team's offensive snaps in the contest, his lowest percentage since Week 1. The wide receiver was briefly sidelined while being evaluated for a head injury before returning to the contest, which likely contributed to his lower workload. Coleman will continue to be an unpredictable fantasy option in Week 11 versus the Dolphins.

Braswell has been ruled out for the remainder of Thursday's game versus the Colts with a knee injury. Braswell suffered an injury in kick coverage on the opening kickoff and was promptly carted off the field with his right leg in an air cast, per James Boyd of The Athletic. The Texans will have to try to find a way to replace his production on special teams.

Daniels completed 23 of 33 passes for 249 yards with three touchdowns and two interceptions and rushed 11 times for 28 yards in the Commanders' 24-21 win over the Giants on Thursday. It was a up-and-down night for Daniels in the narrow division win, as the third-year quarterback's pair of fourth-quarter interceptions threatened to derail Washington's fortunes. Daniels had the Commanders up by a 17-14 score just past the midway point of the third quarter after tossing one- and 31-yard touchdown passes to Ben Sinnott and Antonio Williams, respectively. However, Daniels subsequently squandered one scoring opportunity by throwing interceptions on back-to-back possessions in the fourth quarter, the first at the Giants' two-yard line. He ultimately made up for it with his game-winning 32-yard scoring strike to Stefon Diggs, marking the quarterback's first three-TD-pass tally of the season. Daniels is up to 1,499 passing yards and a 10:2 TD:INT alongside 280 rushing yards and another pair of scores heading into a Week 11 home matchup against the Bengals on Monday night, Nov. 23.

Sinnott caught all four of his targets for 42 yards and a touchdown Thursday in a 24-21 victory against the Giants. Sinnott gave the Commanders a lead just before halftime when he reeled in a one-yard touchdown from Jayden Daniels. It was his first TD of the season and the third of his career. Sinnott's four grabs came out of nowhere, as he'd logged just one catch on two targets through his first eight games of the season. He also ranked third among Washington tight ends Thursday with 24 offensive snaps -- behind Chig Okonkwo (41) and John Bates (28) -- so fantasy managers probably don't need to go rushing to the waiver wire to pick him up. With that said, Sinnott may have earned himself more opportunities with Thursday's effort.

McConkey (back) is listed as active for Sunday's game against the Jets. Though he wasn't among the Chargers' Week 9 inactives, back spasms led to McConkey not recording any snaps during the team's 44-22 loss to the Texans on Nov. 8.  After not traveling to Baltimore with his teammates for this past Monday's 23-20 win, the wideout was able to practice in a limited fashion Wednesday through Friday before carrying a 'questionable' designation into the weekend. With no known setbacks since, the 2024 second-rounder will give it a go and is on track to reclaim his key role in Los Angeles' WR corps alongside Quentin Johnston and Tre' Harris. In the six games he's taken the field in, McConkey has averaged 2.8 catches (on 4.2 targets) for 47.7 yards with one TD, a pace that the 6-foot, 185-pounder figures to pick up if he can avoid injuries in the coming weeks.

Penix completed 23 of 43 passes for 286 yards with no touchdowns and one interception and rushed four times for 29 yards in the Falcons' 35-13 loss to the Chiefs on Sunday. He also fumbled once but recovered. Penix struggled while the game was still in question, but he did manage to pad his stats some down the stretch as the Falcons unsuccessfully tried to overcome their deficit. Penix connected with eight different targets overall on the afternoon, and he ultimately finished with a season high in passing yards. Penix has now tossed six interceptions in the last three games, however, and he'll look to regroup during the Week 11 bye before tackling a difficult matchup against the Vikings on the road on Sunday, Nov. 29.

Williams completed 22 of 37 passes for 279 yards, two touchdowns and four interceptions in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Buccaneers. He also rushed five times for 16 yards. Williams looked unstoppable early, capping Chicago's two first-quarter drives with touchdown passes of nine yards to Rome Odunze and 56 yards to Luther Burden, the latter of whom later exited due to a concussion. The 2024 first overall pick cooled down after that, throwing three second-quarter interceptions en route to a career-worst four interceptions overall. Chicago's defense picked up the slack with a pick-six against Baker Mayfield, and Williams found Colston Loveland for a 38-yard gain to set up Cairo Santos' game-winning field goal on the game's final play. The Bears have reeled off four consecutive wins since Williams returned from a hamstring injury to improve to 7-2, and he didn't have a turnover in the previous three games prior to Sunday night's downturn. Williams will look to clean up the errors in Week 11 against the Saints following Chicago's Week 10 bye.

Odunze caught four of seven targets for 60 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Buccaneers. Odunze bobbled what should have been an easy touchdown catch and failed to get down inbounds by the time he secured the ball, but he made amends two plays later with his first touchdown catch of the season to cap Chicago's opening drive from nine yards out. He had another critical drop later in the game but still finished second on the team behind Luther Burden (concussion) in targets, catches and receiving yards. Burden exited late in the game, and if Chicago's Week 10 bye doesn't provide the team's leading receiver enough time to clear concussion protocol, Odunze could get an uptick in opportunities in Week 11 against the Saints.

Corley caught all three of his targets for 37 yards in addition to returning two kicks for 51 yards during Cleveland's win over the Texans on Sunday. Corley had not caught a pass across the first nine games of the campaign before hauling in three passes during Sunday's victory. He ended up finishing the contest third on the team in receiving yards behind Harold Fannin and Jerry Jeudy.

Williams caught two passes for 27 yards on two targets in Sunday's 30-10 loss to the Vikings. As he's been doing since making his season debut in Week 6, Williams operated as the Packers' third receiver against Minnesota. He logged 20 offensive snaps and ran 16 routes on 37 dropbacks. Williams has yet to hit 50 receiving yards in any of his five games this season and has no real fantasy appeal in 12-team fantasy leagues. He's well behind Matthew Golden, Christian Watson and Tucker Kraft in the order for touches and targets.

Mondon (ankle) is inactive for Sunday's matchup against Pittsburgh. Mondon was deemed doubtful entering the weekend after not practicing Thursday or Friday following Philadelphia's Week 10 bye. He could have seen more action on defense after Zack Baun (back) landed on IR on Saturday, but Mondon will instead miss his first game of the campaign. Jeremiah Trotter and Jihaad Campbell figure to be the Eagles' starting inside linebackers Sunday.

The Giants elevated Mafah from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday, Dan Salomone of the team's official site reports. It's the second time this season that Mafah has been promoted to the 53-man roster, with the first instance being Week 10 against the Eagles. His elevation gives the Giants another contributor on special teams and extra depth in the backfield behind Cam Skattebo, Devin Singletary and Greg Desrosiers.

Cooper caught just two of eight targets for 25 yards in Sunday's 19-11 loss to the Giants. With DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) still out, Cooper played more than 90 percent of the offensive snaps for the third straight game. He's done very little with that playing time, producing five catches for 61 yards during that span. Cooper is well off the fantasy radar until he shows something in the box score, and that's if Smith and Wicks remain sidelined.

Waxter (ankle) is active for Sunday's game against the Jets. Waxter was cleared to return from a one-game absence due to an ankle injury. His availability gives the Chargers another contributor on special teams and depth in the secondary.

Briningstool caught one of two targets for 20 yards in Sunday's 35-13 win against the Jets on Sunday. Briningstool connected with Patrick Mahomes for a 20-yard reception midway through the first quarter but didn't record another reception. The 23-year-old tight end has exactly one catch in each of his past three games. That's not enough production to warrant fantasy consideration, but Briningstool is at least showing growth as a pass catcher, as he had just one catch on two targets over his first six contests of the campaign.

McMillan caught three of seven targets for 35 yards in Sunday's 20-17 win over New Orleans. The seven targets led the Panthers on the afternoon, but the second-year wideout wasn't able to do much with them. The 35 yards were McMillan's lowest total since Week 3, and he'll take a 49-660-3 line on 78 targets through nine games into a Week 11 tilt against the Ravens.

Loveland caught four of six targets for 54 yards in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Buccaneers. Loveland was quiet for most of the night but got free for a 38-yard catch in the final minute to set up Cairo Santos' game-winning 38-yard field goal on the game's final play. The 2025 first-round pick has recorded at least 54 receiving yards in five of the past six games, having bounced back from a slow start to his sophomore season during which Loveland compiled just 34 yards through three games. Loveland will try to keep building momentum in Week 11 against the Saints following Chicago's Week 10 bye.

Warren brought in one of five targets for 22 yards in the Colts' 26-3 loss to the Texans on Thursday. The talented tight end's production continued to suffer collateral damage from Daniel Jones' poor play, but Warren did provide a useful gain on his one catch. The 2025 first-round pick now has recorded Thursday's yardage total or less in three of the last four games, but Warren's outlook may change if Jones, who James Boyd of The Athletic reports head coach Shane Steichen wouldn't rule out demoting when asked after the game, is replaced by Anthony Richardson or Riley Leonard under center.

Williams failed to haul in his lone target during the Patriots' 35-10 loss to the Lions on Sunday in Munich. Williams did have a 21-yard carry late in the third quarter, although the play was nullified by offsetting penalties. It was the second straight game that the second-year wide receiver did not record a catch and the fifth time in 10 regular-season contests. New England is on a bye for Week 11, but the offense's outlook looks grim given that franchise quarterback Drake Maye is expected to miss time due to an ankle injury that he sustained in the first quarter of Sunday's game. The Patriots' next game takes place in Week 12 against the Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 29.

Bryant caught four of five targets for 56 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 26-21 win over Carolina. Bryant was activated from IR on Saturday after recovering from an ankle injury, and he came up big late in Sunday's contest, hauling in a 26-yard TD strike from Bo Nix with less than six minutes left in the fourth quarter for what proved to be the game-winning score. The second-year wideout's clutch play came after Jaylen Waddle (concussion) had left the game, and if a Week 10 bye doesn't give him enough time to recover, Bryant could see an elevated role in Week 11 against the Raiders.

The Cardinals placed Burch (knee) on injured reserve Tuesday. This move was a foregone conclusion, as head coach Mike LaFleur said Monday that Burch will miss the remainder of the campaign after suffering an MCL injury to his left knee. The defensive end finished his sophomore NFL season with 19 tackles, including 1.0 sacks, over 10 games. Burch will now look to get healthy in the hope of being ready for the 2027 campaign.

Winston (shoulder) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Cowboys. Winston's practice reps were limited Thursday due to a shoulder issue, but he was a full participant in Friday's session, which was enough for him to avoid an injury tag heading into the weekend. The second-year safety has 56 tackles (31 solo), one forced fumble and one fumble recovery across seven regular-season games.

Johnson carried the ball 10 times for 42 yards in Sunday's 30-10 loss to the Vikings. The former Steeler led the Packers' backfield in totes and rushing yards, with MarShawn Lloyd chipping in 39 scrimmage yards on seven touches. Johnson has produced modest but decent numbers over the last two games, averaging a 4.6 YPC on 24 carries as the top early-down option for Green Bay. Josh Jacobs (finger) could return after the team's Week 11 bye, but if he isn't cleared, Johnson could find himself atop the depth chart again in Week 12 against the Rams.

Parrish (back) has been ruled out for the rest of Sunday's game against the Lions. Parrish's back injury is severe enough for him to be sidelined for the rest of Sunday's contest. Benjamin Morrison will continue to operate in an elevated role in the secondary in Parrish's absence.

Smith (hamstring) is active for Thursday night's game against the Colts. The cornerback was activated from injured reserve earlier in the day Thursday and will be making his first appearance since Week 4. Smith played just seven defensive snaps across the first four games of the season.
questionable questionable

Felton is on track to operate in a more prominent role in Week 11 versus the 49ers, Kevin Seifert of ESPN.com reports. Felton drew a start in Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers, reeling in a season-high three of five targets for 33 yards over 56 offensive snaps. The wide receiver stepped into a starting role as a result of Jordan Addison (thumb) and Jauan Jennings (calf) being sidelined, and Addison is now reportedly set to undergo surgery to address his injury, opening the door for more opportunities for Felton moving forward.

Carter posted six tackles (two solo) and a defensed pass in Sunday's 38-18 win over Pittsburgh. Carter's tackle tally tied for second-most on the Bengals. The second-year pro has now reached the six-tackle mark in all but one of his nine games this season. Carter leads the Bengals with 74 stops overall, and he's recorded 1.5 sacks, five defensed passes (including an interception) and two forced fumbles.

Sampson rushed four times for six yards and caught four of six targets for 31 yards in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Texans. Sampson hardly carries the ball for Cleveland and is merely the pass-catching complement to Quinshon Judkins out of the backfield. Across five games this season, Sampson has rushed 19 times for 79  yards while adding 16 catches for 152 yards on 22 targets. He's playable in PPR fantasy leagues as a desperation RB2 option, particularly in games for which the Browns are projected to play from behind.
inactive inactive

Watkins caught two passes for 49 yards on three targets in Sunday's 46-40 win over the Cowboys. With Deebo Samuel still working his way back to 100 percent off his hamstring injury, Keenan Allen being eased in after his acquisition from the Colts and Mike Evans (Achilles) remaining inactive, Watkins' 44 snaps led San Francisco's wideouts. However, his three targets were a distant fourth on the team and represented just a 10.7 percent share. Allen will likely play more moving forward, and Evans is expected back in the bear future. Watkins doesn't have much fantasy appeal as an ancillary option.

Phillips underwent surgery on his injured bicep Wednesday, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports. Phillips was recently placed on injured reserve with a season-ending biceps injury sustained in Week 10 versus the Colts. The 22-year-old ends his season with 28 tackles (11 solo) through nine games. Kenneth Grant and Keith Cooper are top candidates to see more reps at defensive tackle as the season continues.

James (calf) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Vikings in Mexico City. James' practice reps were limited both Thursday and Friday due to a calf injury. He was limited to kickoff return duties against the Cowboys in Week 10, and that role could be taken over by Deebo Samuel and/or Jacob Cowing if James is unable to play Sunday.

Giddens rushed one time for five yards and caught his lone target for 11 yards in Thursday night's 26-3 loss to the Texans. With Seth McGowan (hamstring) exiting early with an injury, Giddens spelled Jonathan Taylor and played seven offensive snaps. Through three games this season, Giddens has rushed seven times for 48 yards and registered one catch for 11 yards. If McGowan's injury costs him time, Giddens figures to handle RB2 duties in his absence.

Trader (shoulder/groin) is inactive for Sunday's Week 11 tilt against Buffalo. Trader's inactive status is not surprising given that he didn't practice all week and entered the weekend tagged as doubtful to suit up. Sunday will mark the second-year pro's first career absence. Kyle Louis and/or Zayne Anderson could get a big bump in work at safety in Trader's stead.

players.comment: Lambert-Smith (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Jets. With Ladd McConkey (back) active, Lambert-Smith will be a healthy scratch for Sunday's contest. Lambert-Smith's next opportunity to suit up is Week 12 against the Patriots on Nov. 29, although his path to playing time is limited unless there is an injury in front of him on the Chargers' wide receiver depth chart.

Gadsden hauled in his lone target for seven yards in Monday's 23-20 win over Baltimore. Gadsden went to the locker room during the first half of Monday's game after being poked in the ye, but the second-year tight end was cleared to return for the second quarter. However, his 12 offensive snaps were his lowest since Week 1 against the Cardinals (10), and that lack of playing time coincided with the return of veteran tight end David Njoku, who missed the Chargers' six prior games while on IR due to a fibula injury. Njoku and Charlie Kolar appear to be the Chargers' top options at tight end, squeezing Gadsden out of the game plan ahead of Week 11 against the Jets on Sunday.

Hawes (shoulder) is active for Sunday's game against the Dolphins. Hawes was in danger of missing this contest due to a shoulder issue, though he will avoid his first absence of the 2026 campaign Sunday versus Miami. With Dalton Kincaid (thumb) sidelined in Week 11, Hawes will have an opportunity to get more involved than usual behind Dawson Knox.

Borregales made his sole field-goal attempt and one PAT in the Patriots' 35-10 loss to the Lions in Munich on Sunday. Borregales made a 33-yard field goal on the first drive of the game. The kicker is now 11-for-13 on field-goal attempts and 24-for-25 on PATs through 10 regular-season games in 2026.

players.comment: Howard (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Steelers' emergency quarterback against the Eagles on Sunday. As has been the case all year, Howard will be the emergency QB3 behind starter Aaron Rodgers and backup Mason Rudolph. As such, Howard is not allowed to see the field Sunday unless both Rodgers and Rudolph leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

players.comment: The Colts announced Friday that Leonard will act as Anthony Richardson's backup at quarterback, Stephen Holder of ESPN.com reports. The Colts released starting quarterback Daniel Jones after a disastrous 26-3 Thursday night loss to the Texans in Week 11. With Richardson in line to start moving forward, Leonard is the next QB up on the depth chart. The second-year pro has been with the Colts since 2025, when he played in five games, completing 39 of 67 attempts for 415 yards, two touchdowns and three interceptions. He also rushed six times for 27 yards and two touchdowns.

Brooks carried three times for 12 yards while taking the field for three of the Bengals' 66 offensive snaps in Sunday's 38-18 win over the Steelers. All three of Brooks' carries came during the Bengals' final possession of the fourth quarter, when the team had already built a sizable lead and opted to rest multiple key players, including top running back Chase Brown. Brooks has been active for all nine of the Bengals' games to date but has logged just six carries, all of which have come late in blowout victories. So long as Brown and Samaje Perine are both available, Brooks will continue to see limited playing time on offense.

Bartholomew should revert to a backup role with T.J. Hockenson returning from a wrist injury for Sunday's game against the 49ers, Craig Peters of the Vikings' official site reports. Bartholomew was targeted four times in Week 10 for three catches, 36 yards and a touchdown in the Vikings' 30-10 win over the Packers. The tight end received more than one target in only one other game this season, Week 5, when Hockenson went down after two offensive snaps. While Bartholomew has proven himself a red-zone threat, Hockenson should return to seeing most of the tight end volume in Sunday's contest.

Monangai (toe) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's game against the Saints. After being listed as full on all three of the Bears' Week 11 practice reports, Monangai officially is in the clear for his first game action since Week 4, when he initially suffered a right thumb issue and a turf toe injury. While working in tandem with fellow RB D'Andre Swift this season, Monangai has racked up 60 carries for 324 yards and three touchdowns and caught all five targets for 39 yards in four appearances.

Johnson caught two passes for 76 yards on five targets in Sunday night's 27-24 loss to the Bears. Johnson accounted for the Bucs' longest play of the game, producing a 58-yard catch-and-run to lead the team in receiving yards. Johnson has been working as the Bucs' WR3 behind Emeka Egbuka and Chris Godwin, with rookie Ted Hurst mixing in for sub-package snaps. Johnson isn't a particularly exciting fantasy bet.

Allen (hamstring) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Giants. Allen has next to no fantasy appeal having played a total of 73 offensive snaps this season. In nine games, he's touched the ball a total of three times on offense.

Lohner (foot) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Raiders, Aric DiLalla of the Broncos' official site reports. The Broncos opened Lohner's 21-day practice window Wednesday. The tight end is not quite ready to make his season debut, as he is still tending to his recovery from a foot injury he sustained in the offseason. Lohner was a full participant in all three Week 11 prep sessions, meaning his odds of returning in Week 12 are quite good if he can continue to log full sessions.

Croskey-Merritt (groin) is slated to be activated from IR in time to play in Monday's game against the Bengals, Matt Zenitz of CBS Sports reports. Croskey-Merritt has missed the Commanders' last four games while on injured reserve due to a groin injury. He logged a trio of full practices this week and is officially questionable to play Monday, but it sounds like he'll be activated from IR ahead of the contest and make his return against the Bengals. During Croskey-Merritt's absence, Rachaad White has taken on a larger role in the backfield, but White is currently dealing with a heel injury and is also questionable to suit up Monday.

Biggers (knee) was placed on injured reserve by the Dolphins on Tuesday. Biggers suffered a lateral meniscus tear in Week 10, and he will now miss the remainder of the 2026 campaign while on IR. Fellow defensive lineman Jordan Phillips (biceps) was also placed on IR on Tuesday, and as a result, Kenneth Grant will operate as the team's top dog at defensive tackle moving forward this season.

Fitzgerald made two of his three field-goal attempts and both PATs in the Panthers' 20-17 win over the Saints on Sunday. Fitzgerald's 54-yard field goal as time expired iced the game for the Panthers. The kicker made another field goal from 55 yards while also missing his first attempt of the night from 48 yards out. Fitzgerald moves to 15-for-17 on field-goal attempts and 18-for-23 on PATs so far during the 2026 regular season.

Armstrong caught his only target for a 43-yard touchdown in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Falcons. The wideout played just 17 of 64 offensive snaps against Atlanta and ran only seven pass routes on Patrick Mahomes' 38 dropbacks. Armstrong was tasked with blocking duties on 10 of his snaps. He still managed to catch his first career touchdown in the fourth quarter with the game already well out of hand. Armstrong is not on the fantasy radar.

Green (forearm) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Giants. Green has strung together six consecutive full practices since being designated to return from injured reserve Nov. 11. He's not quite ready to be activated from IR, so his next chance to play is Week 12 against the Titans on Sunday, Nov. 29. Green is in the final stages of his recovery from an elbow injury that he suffered in Week 1 against the Browns.

Cook was signed to the Dolphins' active roster Tuesday. Cook served as the team's No. 2 option at quarterback behind Kyle McCord in the team's 24-22 loss to the Colts in Week 10, with Malik Willis (abdomen) being placed on injured reserve prior to the contest. Cook reverted to the practice squad Monday, but he has now officially become a member of the team's active roster ahead of Sunday's matchup with the Bills.

The Raiders elevated Runyon from the practice squad Saturday. Las Vegas is bringing up Runyon due to Brock Bowers (ankle) being listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Broncos. Runyon appeared in 13 games with the Raiders last season but logged just 45 offensive snaps and caught only one pass for three yards. He's depth behind Michael Mayer and Ian Thomas.

Price is set for an increase in offensive workload with Jordan Addison (thumb) sidelined, Kevin Seifert of ESPN.com reports. Price reeled in a season-high four passes for 49 yards and a score during Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers. The wideout was operating in a more prominent offensive role for the second week in a row with Jauan Jennings (calf) sidelined, and fellow wide receiver Jordan Addison (thumb) was unable to play as well. Addison now is expected to undergo thumb surgery, opening the door for Price to operate in an elevated position in Minnesota's offense for the time being.

Restrepo, whom the Titans signed off their practice squad Tuesday, could be in store for more playing time out of the slot moving forward after Tennessee placed Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) on injured reserve, Mark Mihalko of USA Today reports. A 2025 undrafted free agent who played alongside Cam Ward during their final collegiate seasons at Miami, Restrepo showed immediate chemistry with the Titans' second-year quarterback during a 40-23 loss to the Jaguars in Week 10. Restrepo went on to play 19 snaps following Robinson's exit late in the third quarter and notched three receptions for 31 yards on three targets over the game's final 10 minutes. While the Titans are expected to get rookie first-round pick Carnell Tate (shoulder) back for Sunday's game in Dallas, Restrepo's strong showing in relief of the injured Robinson last week should at least allow him to stick ahead of Calvin Ridley (four snaps in Week 10) as Tennessee's No. 4 wideout.

The Chiefs elevated Carter from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday, Matt Derrick of ChiefsDigest.com reports. Carter has been brought up from the practice squad for a second consecutive week to give the Chiefs more depth in the backfield in the absence of Kenneth Walker (groin). Carter operated as the Chiefs' RB2 behind rookie fifth-rounder Emmett Johnson in Week 10 against the Falcons, but the former's role could be limited to special-teams duties since Jaydn Ott (hamstring) has been cleared to return from a one-game absence.

Kiner carried the ball 10 times for 25 yards in Sunday's 35-10 loss to Detroit. Rhamondre Stevenson was active despite dealing with a knee issue during the practice week, but the veteran back gained just four yards on six carries, and Kiner wound up leading the Patriots' backfield in both volume and yardage. The entire offense struggles after Drake Maye (ankle) was knocked out of the game early, however. New England gets a Week 11 bye, so Kiner's role and usage for a Week 12 clash with the Chargers likely won't become clear until the health of Stevenson and Maye come into focus after the break.

Chism did not catch his only target during the Patriots' 35-10 loss against the Lions in Munich in Week 10. A.J. Brown (hamstring) returned from a two-game absence caused by ankle and knee injuries in Week 10, and as a result, Chism saw his lowest snap count this season (8) since he was a healthy scratch in Week 1. His role coming out of the Patriots' bye in Week 11 will probably depend heavily on the availability of Brown, who picked up a hamstring issue against the Lions.

Larison turned his lone carry into two yards and caught two of three targets for 15 yards and a touchdown during the Patriots' 35-10 loss to the Lions on Sunday in Munich. He also recorded a tackle on special teams. The Patriots lost starting quarterback Drake Maye to an ankle injury early in the first quarter, so backup Tommy DeVito was under center for most of contest. New England struggled with DeVito at the helm, but he did connect with Larison for a 10-yard touchdown pass early in the fourth quarter in what was the Patriots' lone trip to the end zone. Even though that score came in garbage time, it was the first touchdown of Larison's NFL career, although he's firmly entrenched as the team's RB3 behind Rhamondre Stevenson and Corey Kiner. The Patriots are on a bye for Week 11, so their next game will take place in Week 12 against the Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 29.

Schwesinger logged 13 tackles (eight solo) in the Browns' 27-24 win over the Texans on Sunday. Schwesinger continues to be a model of consistency, having played all 658 defensive snaps for the Browns in 2026. The middle linebacker has logged double-digit tackles in six of the team's 10 contests so far, adding 3.0 sacks and three forced fumbles over that span.

Thornton is dealing with a back injury, but he wasn't listed on Las Vegas' practice report during Week 11 prep. As such, it appears the second-year wideout is a healthy scratch Sunday. Tre Tucker, Jalen Nailor, Jack Bech, Dareke Young and Cody White will make up the Raiders' WR corps.

The Eagles signed Blue from their practice squad to their active roster Tuesday. It's already the third time this season Blue has been signed by Philadelphia from the practice squad to the active roster. The second-year pro has seen action in two games with the club, recording a nine-yard catch on his only touch while racking up 268 yards on 12 kickoff returns. Blue is currently the only healthy running back on the Eagles' active roster aside from starter Saquon Barkley, but that may change soon, as Will Shipley (foot - IR) had his practice window opened Monday. Elijah Mitchell has been promoted from the practice squad to help in the backfield each of the past three weeks, so he'd need to be signed to the active roster as well in order to suit up against Pittsburgh this Sunday.

The Rams are expected to lean more on Mumpfield and the rest of the team's wide receivers in the absence of Puka Nacua (knee/toe), the latter of whom is expected to be sidelined for the remainder of the regular season, Nate Atkins and Jonathan Jones of The Athletic report. Nacua is expected to miss "a couple of months" after undergoing surgery Tuesday to repair his MCL, per Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com. With Nacua and Davante Adams (hamstring, IR) sidelined for Week 10 against the Cardinals, Mumpfield operated as the Rams' WR1 for that contest and finished with three catches (on four targets) for 81 yards in a 34-6 win for Los Angeles. The Rams are "hopeful" that Adams will return soon, but if he's not activated from injured reserve ahead of Wednesday's game against the Packers, then Mumpfield would lead Los Angeles' wide receiver group that also includes Tutu Atwell, CJ Daniels and Xavier Smith.

Etienne took three carries for one yard and caught both of his two targets for nine yards during Sunday's 20-17 win at New Orleans. He also returned three punts for 43 yards. Etienne again played second fiddle to starter Chuba Hubbard in Week 10 with Jonathon Brooks sidelined by a groin injury, and Etienne got his second-most touches of the season. His role on offense in Week 11 will depend on Brooks' status, but the vast majority of the Panthers' snaps at tailback will continue to go to Hubbard.

Simon (calf) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Chiefs. Simon is being evaluated by medical staff to determine whether he can return to Sunday's contest. His absence gives the Cardinals less depth at linebacker behind Jack Gibbens, Mack Wilson and Zaven Collins.

Horton failed to garner a target during Sunday's 21-13 win over the Raiders. Horton failed to reel in a pass for the first time since Week 7, and his 10 offensive snaps ranked fourth at wide receiver for Seattle behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba (43), Cooper Kupp (35) and Rashid Shaheed (25). Horton will continue to be an unappealing fantasy option as long as he's buried below the other three wideouts on the depth chart.

Fannin brought in seven of nine targets for 91 yards in the Browns' 27-24 win over the Texans on Sunday. Fannin led the Browns across the board in receptions, receiving yards and targets, and his 30-yard grab on Cleveland's penultimate possession set up Quinshon Judkins' game-winning five-yard touchdown rush on the next play. Fannin's chemistry with Deshaun Watson has been outstanding, and the second-year tight end now has at least 91 receiving yards in three of the past four games. Fannin will remain a central figure in Cleveland's impressive air attack when the team returns to action in a home matchup against the Raiders on Sunday, Nov. 29, following a Week 11 bye.

Offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel told reporters Friday that his "expectation" is that Hampton is the lead back for the Chargers, Omar Navarro of the team's official site reports. "Generally, my expecation is [Hampton] is our leading ball carrier every week.  ... I knew based on his last two practice weeks, we were feeling like he was going to have a breakout performance at any given time," McDaniel said Friday. That breakout game took place Monday against the Ravens, when Hampton turned 22 carries into a season-high 105 yards and a touchdown in a 23-20 win for the Chargers. With the Chargers getting extra time to rest, Hampton's stock is trending up heading into Week 12 against the Jets, whose defense ranks 30th in the NFL in rushing yards allowed per game (135.3) and 29th in rushing touchdowns allowed (13).

Golden caught five of nine targets for 70 yards in Sunday's 30-10 loss to the Vikings. The second-year wideout was the only Packer to have much success on offense, leading the team in catches, targets and receiving yards. Golden has reached 70 yards in three straight games and five of the last six, and he heads into a Week 11 bye with a 58-853-5 line on 101 targets through 10 contests. His next chance to add to those numbers will come in Week 12 against the Rams.

TeSlaa caught two of five targets for 19 yards and a touchdown during the Lions' 35-10 win over the Patriots on Sunday in Munich. He also recorded a tackle. It was a quiet day for TeSlaa, with the Lions' offense being powered by usual suspects Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jahmyr Gibbs, with the latter duo combining for four touchdowns (three receiving, one rushing). TeSlaa was the other Lions player to find the end zone, which took place early in the second quarter on a 12-yard touchdown pass from Jared Goff. It was the first touchdown catch of the season for TeSlaa, who found the end zone six times across 17 regular-season games during his rookie campaign in 2025. He has been the Lions' distant WR3 behind St. Brown and Jameson Williams, and that shouldn't change ahead of the team's Week 11 tilt against the Buccaneers on Nov. 22.

Williams recorded five total tackles (two solo) and two passes defensed, including an interception, during Sunday's 35-13 win over the Falcons. Williams was able to register at least five takedowns for the third time this season, and his biggest moment of the game came in the fourth quarter when he intercepted a deep pass from Falcons quarterback Michael Penix. The interception was his second of the year, and he has now compiled 41 total tackles (23 solo) and 11 passes defensed over nine contests so far during the 2026 campaign.

Dike caught two passes for 16 yards on three targets in Sunday's 40-23 loss to the Jaguars. He added five rushing yards on one attempt. With Carnell Tate (shoulder) out again, Dike played 54 of 57 offensive snaps against Jacksonville, but his three targets were a distant fifth on the team and represented just an 8.1 percent target share. Outside of his 5-71-1 receiving outburst in Week 8 against Cincinnati, Dike has amassed eight catches for 69 scoreless yards. He's not a reliable fantasy option, though a Week 11 date with Dallas' secondary awaits should Tate remain sidelined.

Nolen (illness) was a full participant in practice Thursday, Zach Gershman of the Cardinals' official site reports. The defensive tackle was not able to practice Wednesday due to an illness. Now that he's back, he should be able to play Sunday against the Chiefs. Nolen has played on a majority of the defensive snaps in each game he's been available for this season, recording 25 tackles (eight solo), including 1.0 sacks.

Campbell (hamstring/quadriceps) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice. Campbell was sidelined for each of the Eagles' two contests prior to the Week 10 bye due to hamstring and quadriceps injuries. The second-year linebacker made the most of the extra rest courtesy of the bye, and he is on track to return against the Steelers on Sunday.

The 49ers activated West (knee) from injured reserve Saturday. The Niners also removed West's questionable tag, so he should be ready to play Sunday night against Minnesota. West played 41 percent of the defensive snaps during the first two weeks of the season before suffering his knee injury.

Hunter caught both of his targets for 16 yards, recorded a three-yard carry and contributed five tackles (three solo) and an interception during the Jaguars' 40-23 win over the Titans on Sunday. Fifty-six of Hunter's 62 snaps Sunday came on defense, and that's where he made his biggest impact with a diving interception on a Cam Ward pass intended for Elic Ayomanor, and the Jaguars offense converted that takeaway into a field goal 10 plays later. Hunter's impact on both sides of the ball has been undeniable: he has 28 catches (on 45 targets) for 298 yards and a touchdown, along with 36 tackles (24 solo) and seven pass defenses (including three interceptions) through nine regular-season games. The Jaguars will hit the road for Week 11 against the Giants on Nov. 22.

Tuten (ankle/foot) was present for the stretching portion of Friday's practice before moving to a side field, Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union reports. Tuten was deemed limited at practice Wednesday and then was a non-participant Thursday. It remains to be seen how the Jaguars classify his participation (or lack thereof) in Friday's session, with added clarity on that front set to arrive via the team's upcoming injury report.

Green racked up six tackles (four solo), including 2.0 sacks, in Monday's Week 10 loss to the Chargers. Green's first sack came late in the second quarter, and he brought down Chargers QB Justin Herbert again early in the fourth. After registering 3.5 sacks in 17 regular-season games as a rookie last year, Green has already exceeded that mark with 5.5 sacks through 10 contests this season. His six total tackles in Week 10 also tied his career-high mark.

Sanders (shoulder) is inactive for Sunday's game against Miami. Sanders logged a full practice Wednesday, though he posted limited sessions on Thursday and Friday. After carrying a questionable designation ahead of Sunday's meeting with the Dolphins, he has been ruled out, meaning his next opportunity to get back on the field will come in Week 12 versus the Chiefs.

Ezeiruaku (ankle) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Titans, Tommy Yarrish of the Cowboys' official site reports. Ezeiruaku didn't play against the 49ers in Week 10 due to an ankle injury. He's avoided an injury tag for Week 11 after logging a full practice Friday, and his return means less rotational snaps at the edge rusher position will be available for James Houston and Von Miller. Ezeiruaku has 32 tackles (16 solo), including 2.5 sacks, and one forced fumble across nine regular-season games.

Harris secured all five targets for 86 yards in the Chargers' 23-20 win over the Ravens on Monday night. With Ladd McConkey (back) sidelined, Harris functioned as a de facto top target for Justin Herbert, and he was responsible for all but 43 of his quarterback's passing yards. The yardage tally also was a career-high figure for Harris, who generated team-high totals with all three components of his receiving line. Harris is up to a career-high 348 receiving yards on 26 catches heading into a favorable Week 11 home matchup against the Jets on Sunday.

Bech caught two of seven targets for 10 yards during the Raiders' 21-13 loss to the Seahawks on Sunday. Bech was the favorite target of rookie first-overall pick Fernando Mendoza, who was making his first career start Sunday after the Raiders shipped Kirk Cousins to the Vikings at the Nov. 10 trade deadline. Bech's seven targets were a season high, but he mustered only two catches for his efforts, and he failed to connect on each of the last four passes he saw from Mendoza in the fourth quarter. The volume appears to be there for Bech, and he could take on a larger role offensively in Week 11 against the Broncos on Nov. 22 if star tight end Brock Bowers (ankle) is unable to play.

Bears head coach Ben Johnson confirmed Tuesday that Burden has cleared concussion protocol, Patrick Finley of the Chicago Sun-Times reports. Burden's status was up in the air for a bit with the Bears going on bye immediately after he sustained a concussion in a Week 9 win over the  Buccaneers, but he was spotted working out on the field with teammates Monday and has apparently cleared all five phases of the protocol. The second-year wideout looks like he'll be a full practice participant throughout Week 11, and he shouldn't face any playing-time limitations in Sunday's game versus the Saints.

With Omar Cooper (ankle) ruled out, coach Aaron Glenn said Friday that Taylor could see more pass-catching opportunities Sunday against the Chargers. Isaiah Williams (ribs) also has been ruled out for the Jets, so they'll be down their Nos. 3 and 4 receivers, which could lead to more multiple-tight end sets for New York. Taylor is averaging 2.8 catches for 20.9 yards per game this season. He's a touchdown-or-bust fantasy bet.

Ferguson (hamstring/ankle) isn't ready to return to game action, but the Rams still plan to activate him from injured reserve before Week 12 and keep him on the active roster, Adam Grosbard of The Orange County Register reports. Even if Ferguson is moved back to the active roster, coach Sean McVay's comments indicate the tight end still won't be ready to play coming out of the team's Week 11 bye. His activation at least would keep him off season-ending IR, but his near-term availability remains uncertain until the Rams signal he's ready for game action. With Puka Nacua (knee/toe) likely done for the remainder of the regular season following MCL surgery, Ferguson and Davante Adams (hamstring) are needed badly in this offense.

Knight finished with eight tackles (six solo) and a defensed pass against the Steelers in a 38-18 victory Sunday. Knight led Cincinnati in tackles in the blowout win. The second-year linebacker has recorded exactly eight stops in four of his past five games, and he's finished with at least that tally in all but three of his appearances overall this season. Knight hasn't yet recorded a sack, but he's on pace to blow by his rookie total of 106 stops, as he has 71 tackles across nine games.

Shough is no longer wearing a protect glove on his left (non-throwing) hand at Thursday's practice, Nick Underhill of NewOrleans.Football reports. The second-year quarterback suffered two broken bones in his left hand back on Oct. 5 and has been playing with the glove ever since. He's also been able to only hand the ball off with his right hand since suffering the injury. Shough has completed 66.8 percent of his passes for 2,173 yards, 15 touchdowns and seven interceptions across nine starts this season. He's averaging one full yard less per pass attempt (6.3) and 1.3 fewer yards per completion (9.5) compared to his 2025 rookie season.

Morrison (hamstring) has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's matchup against Detroit, Scott Smith of the Buccaneers' official site reports. Morrison was ruled out by Tampa Bay during the second half. He'll finish the contest with four tackles (three solo). Jacob Parrish (back) has also been ruled out for the remainder of the game, so Kevin Knowles has entered at cornerback for the Bucs.

Norman-Lott (knee) is inactive against Arizona on Sunday. Norman-Lott was activated from the Chiefs' reserve/PUP list Wednesday, but he was limited in all three practices during Week 11 prep and drew the questionable tag for Sunday's game. He's in the final stages of his recovery from a torn ACL that he sustained in October of 2025, but he's not quite ready to make his return. Norman-Lott's next opportunity to make his 2026 regular-season debut is Thanksgiving Day against the Bills.

Judkins rushed 10 times for 38 yards and a touchdown and brought in three of five targets for 33 yards in the Browns' 27-24 win over the Texans on Sunday. Judkins' rushing volume was at a season-low level, but the second-year back managed to record his fourth rushing touchdown of the campaign on a five-yard run with just under a minute remaining. That proved to be the game-winning score, and Judkins also mustered his second-highest receiving yardage tally of the campaign. The 2025 first-round pick is averaging just 3.4 yards per carry, however, so he remains far from efficient heading into a Week 11 bye ahead of a Week 12 home matchup against the Raiders on Sunday, Nov. 29.

Meyers caught both of his targets for 20 yards and a touchdown while also adding 58 yards as a kick returner during Sunday night's 38-18 win over the Steelers. Meyers reeled in multiple passes for the third straight game, and he was able to secure his first score of the year in the second quarter on a 15-yard touchdown pass from Joe Burrow. The 26-year-old's 28 offensive snaps ranked fourth at wide receiver for Cincinnati behind Ja'Marr Chase (59), Tee Higgins (51) and Colbie Young (29). With Andrei Iosivas (thumb) nearing a return to action, Meyers may see a sharp drop in offensive opportunities in the near future.

Lemon will operate as the Eagles' WR2 against the Steelers on Sunday due to the return of DeVonta Smith (hamstring). Smith has missed five of the Eagles' last six games (and each of the last three contests) due to a hamstring injury, but the veteran wide receiver does not carry an injury designation heading into the weekend. Lemon has been the team's WR1 in Smith's absence, but the former still will be heavily involved in the offensive game plan given that Dontayvion Wicks (ankle/foot) has been ruled out for a fourth consecutive game. Joe Milton is getting the start at quarterback for a second straight contest, and the Eagles are facing a Steelers defense that ranks 30th in the NFL in receiving yards allowed per game (260.6). Over his last five outings, Lemon has put together a 27-247-1 line on 39 targets.

Lane brought in three of 11 targets for 61 yards in the Ravens' 23-20 loss to the Chargers on Monday night. Lane was far from efficient during his first opportunity to work with new quarterback Jacoby Brissett, but he parlayed his career-high target total into a career-best yardage tally. The fact the rookie third-round pick garnered so much of Brissett's attention was certainly encouraging, and Lane could emerge as a much more consistent No. 3 option in the offense in coming weeks.

Barham (hip/groin) is inactive for Sunday's game versus Tennessee. Barham didn't practice on Friday due to hip and groin issues. He was listed as questionable for Sunday's meeting with the Titans, though he has since been ruled out. With the rookie unavailable to play in Week 11, DeMarvion Overshown could see more snaps.

players.comment: Singleton (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Cowboys. Week 11 marks the fifth time in six games that Singleton will be a healthy scratch, despite the fact that Tyjae Spears (knee) was placed on injured reserve Saturday. As such, Michael Carter and Julius Chestnut will operate as the Titans' rotational options in the backfield behind workhorse running back Tony Pollard on Sunday. Singleton's next opportunity to play is Week 12 against the Jaguars on Nov. 29.

Cuevas caught all three of his targets for 37 yards during Monday night's 23-20 loss to the Chargers. Cuevas had an immediate connection with new starting quarterback Jacoby Brissett, reeling in at least three passes for the second time this season and the first time since Week 6. The tight end ranked fourth at his position with 11 offensive snaps, sitting behind Mark Andrews (40), Matthew Hibner (22) and Nick Vannett (14). Cuevas has now caught 13 of 16 targets for 171 yards and a touchdown over 10 contests so far during the 2026 campaign.

players.comment: Randall (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against Carolina. Randall was recently reinstated from injured reserve. However, with Derrick Henry, Justice Hill and Rasheen Ali available versus the Panthers, Randall will be inactive.

Allen caught two of four targets for 44 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Falcons. The rookie wideout scored his first career touchdown by beating the cornerback on a stutter-go for a 39-yard touchdown in the third quarter. With Josh Downs still getting comfortable and learning the offense following Tuesday's acquisition from the Colts, Allen maintained a significant role on offense, playing 22 of 64 offensive snaps. Once Downs progresses from the 10 snaps he played against Atlanta, it will be interesting to see if Allen can push Xavier Worthy (zero catches on three targets across 56 snaps on Sunday) for a larger piece of the outside receiver role in Kansas City's offense.

Smack pushed a 53-yard field-goal try wide right in the first quarter before later converting a 40-yard attempt in the final seconds of the third quarter. The rookie has now gone 15-for-21 on field-goal tries, including 3-for-4 from 50-plus yards, while making 21 of 24 extra-point attempts over 10 contests so far during the 2026 campaign.

The rookie seventh-rounder has yet to appear in a regular-season game in 2026. As the emergency QB3, Nussmeier is prohibited from playing Sunday unless both Patrick Mahomes and Justin Fields leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

Sturdivant caught two passes for 37 yards and a touchdown on four targets in Sunday's 30-10 loss to the Vikings. After Green Bay was shut out in the first half, Sturdivant's first career touchdown came in the third quarter from 32 yards out, and it went down as the Packers' lone touchdown of the afternoon. Sturdivant played just nine offensive snaps as the fourth receiver and would need more than one injury ahead of him on the depth chart to be relevant in fantasy.

Ott (hamstring) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice. Ott was unable to play against the Falcons in Week 10 due to a hamstring injury. However, the undrafted rookie out of Oklahoma was cleared to practice in full Wednesday, so he should be available for Sunday's home game against the Cardinals. If Kenneth Walker (groin) cannot play in Week 11, then Ott would have the opportunity to serve as the Chiefs' RB2 behind rookie fifth-rounder Emmett Johnson.

With Kenneth Walker (groin) ruled out for Sunday's game against the Cardinals, Johnson is in line to handle workhorse duties for the second straight week, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports. There was no sense in pushing Walker to play against a Cardinals team that is injury-ruined and likely to be blown out at Arrowhead. Johnson will get another crack at RB1 duties after he dismantled Atlanta's defense for 171 total yards and two touchdowns on 28 touches last Sunday. He's a top fantasy RB play.

Styles recorded 13 tackles (five solo) during the Commanders' 24-21 win over the Giants on Thursday. Styles once again led the Commanders in stops while playing every single defensive snap. He has logged exactly 13 tackles in four of his last five games and is up to 80 tackles (37 solo), including 1.0 sacks, four pass defenses (including one interception) and one forced fumble through nine regular-season games. Styles' 80 combined tackles are third-most among rookies behind Anthony Hill (neck) (82) and Arvell Reese (81).

Tyson (chest) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's game at Chicago. Tyson opened Week 11 prep with back-to-back limited sessions due to a chest injury, but his return to a full practice Friday has him in the clear for Sunday's matchup. He'll look to build upon the 11-80-0 line on 13 targets the he compiled against the Panthers in Week 10.

With Omar Cooper (ankle) ruled out, coach Aaron Glenn said Friday that Sadiq could see more pass-catching opportunities Sunday against the Chargers. In addition to Cooper, Isaiah Williams (ribs) also will be sidelined against Los Angeles. Sadiq could essentially handle WR3 duties behind Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell, though it's not the easiest matchup against the Los Angeles defense. Sadiq has a chance to see elevated snaps, which could translate to more targets in the passing game, but he's still difficult to get behind as a fantasy starter.

Stribling (ankle) was doing some work on the side at Wednesday's practice, Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com reports. This is the first time Stribling has participated in on-field work since suffering a significant ankle injury in the Week 1 win over the Rams. The expectation has been that the rookie could be back by December, so Stribling is progressing toward hitting that goal. Once Stribling progresses to full-team drills, his timeline will get more dialed in. The 49ers have two more games in November, leaving the Week 13 matchup against the Giants as his earliest potential return date.

Parker accumulated five tackles (three solo), including 2.0 sacks, in the Bills' 31-12 win over the Jets on Sunday. Parker sacked his former Clemson quarterback Cade Klubnik twice in the Bills' blowout win. The rookie second-rounder called his shot, discussing his wishes to sack Klubnik while answering a question from Sal Capaccio of WGR Sports Radio 550 Buffalo in late April.

Boston caught just one pass for 16 yards on two targets in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Texans. The rookie wideout entered play Sunday dealing with a toe injury and appeared to aggravate it versus Houston. At less than 100 percent health, Boston was unproductive in the box score and saw a microscopic five percent target share. After popping back up for 6-98-0 receiving last Sunday in New Orleans with Shedeur Sanders at quarterback, Boston reverted to his sluggish ways with Deshaun Watson in Week 10. Over his last four games with Watson, Boston has compiled 11 catches for 95 empty yards. Boston can't be trusted in fantasy lineups until he shows more consistency.

Allen posted 16 tackles (seven solo) during the Colts' 26-3 loss to the Texans on Thursday. It was a busy night for the rookie second-rounder, who finished with a career-high in stops while logging double-digit tackles for the third time this season. Allen has 45 total tackles over his last four outings, and most of that extra playing time has come in the absence of Akeem Davis-Gaither (knee, IR).

Williams secured both targets for 42 yards and a touchdown in the Commanders' 24-21 win over the Giants on Thursday. Williams was a distant second to Stefon Diggs in receiving yards for the Commanders on the night, but like the latter, the former was on the receiving end of one of Jayden Daniels' three touchdown passes. Williams scored from 31 yards out just past the midway point of the third quarter, his first touchdown since way back in Week 1 against the Eagles. Williams hasn't been able to fully take advantage of the absence of Terry McLaurin (knee, IR) as of yet, but Thursday's score is certainly an encouraging sign heading into a Week 11 home matchup against the Bengals on Monday night, Nov. 23.

Fields brought in three of four targets for 62 yards in the Giants' 24-21 loss to the Commanders on Thursday. The rookie finished a distant second in receiving yards to Isaiah Likely for the Giants on the night, but Fields' yardage total was the second highest of his nascent career. Fields has at least three catches in three consecutive games after opening his career with six straight two-reception efforts, and the Notre Dame product will look to continue cultivating his chemistry with J.J. McCarthy in a Week 11 home matchup against the Jaguars on Sunday, Nov. 22.

Haulcy logged nine tackles (four solo) and an interception during the Colts' 26-3 loss to the Texans on Thursday. The rookie third-rounder recorded the first interception of his career in the first quarter, when a pass from C.J. Stroud intended for Nico Collins bounced off Haulcy's helmet, off the hands of Cam Bynum and into Haulcy's arms. The LSU product is up to 53 tackles (30 solo) and three pass defenses through 10 regular-season games.

Hurst failed to haul in his lone target during the Buccaneers' 27-24 loss to the Bears on Sunday. For a third consecutive game, the rookie third-rounder didn't record a catch while seeing only one target. Of more concern was the fact that Hurst was on the field for only one offensive snap in Week 9 after logging at least 25 offensive snaps in each of the first eight games of the regular season. That lack of offensive playing time coincided with the return of Emeka Egbuka, although Hurst also saw less snaps than Chris Godwin (62), Tez Johnson (52) and even David Sills (six), although Sills was cut by the Buccaneers on Tuesday. With the Buccaneers on a bye for Week 10, Hurst will look for better results in Week 11 against the Lions on Sunday, Nov. 22.

Thomas (ankle) is active for Sunday's matchup against New Orleans. Thomas popped up on the practice report as a nonparticipant Friday due to an ankle issue and was initially deemed questionable for Sunday. However, the rookie will ultimately be able to play through the issue. Thomas typically has a minimal role on offense, as he's caught more than one pass in only one of his nine appearances so far. However, he's worked as Chicago's primary kickoff returner and should again contribute in that role against the Saints.

Klubnik completed 11 of 20 passes for 137 yards, no touchdowns and one interception in Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills. He added three rushing attempts for 26 yards. Klubnik saw the first regular-season action of his NFL career in the second half of Sunday's loss, as Geno Smith (ankle) exited the game. The rookie fourth-round pick led the offense down to Buffalo's four-yard line on his first possession in the third quarter, but the Jets settled for a field goal on that possession, and Klubnik was picked off on his next drive. If Smith isn't ready to return in Week 11, Klubnik would be in line to make his first regular-season start on the road against the Chargers.

Lee (hamstring) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice. Lee missed the Panthers' last two games due to a hamstring injury. However, his full participation in Wednesday's practice indicates that the rookie fourth-rounder has fully recovered from his injury, and Lee should be back on the field for the Panthers against the Ravens on Sunday.

Daniels (Achilles) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Chiefs, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports. Daniels popped up on Thursday's practice report as a limited participant due to an Achilles injury, but his full session Friday was enough for him to avoid an injury tag for Sunday's home game. The rookie fourth-rounder has accumulated 61 tackles (41 solo), including 1.0 sacks, two pass defenses (including one interception) and one fumble recovery through nine regular-season games.

Lance returned three kickoffs for 55 yards during the Saints' 20-17 loss to the Panthers on Sunday. The rookie fourth-rounder didn't see a target from Tyler Shough during Sunday's loss, and Lance has not recorded a catch in each of his last two outings, coinciding with the return of 2026 first-round wide receiver Jordyn Tyson. Lance's nine offensive snaps were a season low, and he figures to be limited to return duties now that Tyson is back in the fold. The Saints will hit the road for Week 11 against the Bears on Nov. 22.

Virgil was on the field for 16 of the Cardinals' 35 offensive snaps (45.7 percent), but the rookie fifth-rounder didn't get a target during Sunday's 34-6 loss to the Rams. The Cardinals' offense struggled in its first game this season with rookie third-rounder Carson Beck under center, finishing with just 17:37 in time of possession. That meant less opportunities for Virgil and the rest of the pass catchers, and even star tight end Trey McBride finished with only five catches on as many targets for 37 yards. It's hard to put much trust into Virgil and the rest of the pass catchers, especially with the team heading into a tough Week 11 road tilt against Kansas City.

Cameron caught all three of his targets for 67 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 40-23, Week 10 win over Tennessee. He also returned five kickoffs for 142 yards. Cameron gave the Jaguars a 14-point lead early in the fourth quarter when he hauled in a 25-yard touchdown pass from Trevor Lawrence. It was the rookie wideout's third touchdown of the campaign but his first since Week 3. Cameron's 67 receiving yards marked a career high, while his three receptions tied the most he's had as a pro. Cameron's propensity for finding the end zone (his three TDs have come on just 12 total catches) is appealing, but at this point he isn't getting enough volume to be a reliable week-to-week fantasy asset.
