McGowan (hamstring) has been ruled out for the rest of Thursday's game against the Texans, Jane Slater of NFL Network reports. McGowan was injured just before halftime while returning a kickoff. He was deemed questionable to return at the beginning of the third quarter and subsequently was ruled out shortly thereafter. The rookie running back gained seven yards on three carries and caught his only target for one yard before exiting while adding 117 yards on three kickoff returns. Jonathan Taylor should continue to get most of the work at running back for the Colts for the rest of the game, and DJ Giddens should handle whatever backfield snaps that Taylor doesn't get.

Burks was targeted three times for zero catches, had one kick return for 10 yards and made one tackle on kick coverage during the Colts' 26-3 loss to the Texans on Thursday night. Burks was the No. 2 wide receiver for the Colts in the contest. Despite being targeted three times, the wide receiver could not haul in any passes from since-cut quarterback Daniel Jones. Burks played 32 offensive snaps and two special-teams snaps in the contest.

Zvada missed his only field-goal try and made all three of his PATs on Thursday in a loss to Washington. Zvada's miss was a chip-shot 33-yarder in the first quarter that sailed wide left. That proved to be a critical mistake, as the Commanders won by just three points. Zvada appeared to shore up his job security a bit by going 4-for-4 on FG tries in Week 9 against Philadelphia, but it's hard to ignore the fact that he's gone just 17-for-23 on field-goal attempts overall and has missed three kicks from under 50 yards. The rookie does have a perfect 16-for-16 mark on extra-point attempts, and head coach John Harbaugh expressed support for the inconsistent kicker Friday, saying of Zvada, "I'm confident that he's going to become a good kicker. If at some point and time it doesn't happen, it doesn't happen. But I'm not going to panic halfway through the season with a guy who has made a bunch of kicks," Dan Duggan of The Athletic reports.

players.comment: King (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the emergency third quarterback against the Ravens on Sunday, Steve Reed of the Associated Press reports. King will only play Sunday if both Bryce Young and Kenny Pickett leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

Stevens made his only field-goal attempt and was successful on all three of his extra-point tries in Thursday's 24-21 win over the Giants. Stevens began the scoring in the contest with a 46-yard field goal early in the second period. That ended up being his only FG try of the game, but he made all three of his PATs. Stevens continued what has been a mostly fine rookie campaign -- he's made 17 of 20 field-goal attempts, with all three of his misses coming from 50-plus yards. However, he's just 15-for-18 on point-after tries.

Daniels is set for his usual role as Tampa Bay's backup quarterback Sunday versus Detroit, as Baker Mayfield (foot/thumb) is active and will start, Scott Smith of the Buccaneers' official site reports. Mayfield entered Sunday deemed questionable due to his injuries, but he's ultimately going to be able to suit up. As such, Daniels will retain his role as Mayfield's backup. Easton Stick (coach's decision) is serving as Tampa Bay's emergency third quarterback.

Donaldson (shoulder) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice. Donaldson missed the Saints' last three games due to a shoulder injury, but his full practice Wednesday indicates that he'll be available for Sunday's road game against the Bears. Even if Donaldson does suit up, his role in the backfield figures to be minimal, seeing as Travis Etienne is off injured reserve and Alvin Kamara and Audric Estime are also available for the Saints.

Wallace recorded a nine-yard reception on his lone target in Sunday's 34-6 loss to the Rams. Though he played just five of the Cardinals' 35 snaps on offense, Wallace was able to come away with his first NFL reception in the third quarter. Even if Wallace earns more playing time in future weeks, he'll likely struggle to produce meaningful fantasy lines while rookie third-round pick Carson Beck continues to direct the offense behind a shaky offensive line.

The Chargers placed Shelley (ankle) on injured reserve Saturday. Shelley was already ruled out for Sunday's game against the Jets due to an ankle injury. His placement on IR means he must miss at least the next four games, so his next opportunity to play is Week 15 against the 49ers on Thursday, Dec. 17. Shelley has contributed both on defense and special teams and has eight solo tackles and a pass defense across six regular-season games.

The Saints placed Miller (knee) on injured reserve Saturday. Miller is dealing with a knee injury and is now required to miss at least four games. The rookie nose tackle has played in four games this season, logging five tackles (two solo) over 93 snaps on defense and four snaps on special teams. Nathan Shepherd and Khristian Boyd could both get more defensive snaps during Miller's absence.

Raridon caught his only target for six yards in Sunday's loss to the Lions in Munich. The rookie tight end played his normal allotment of plays, seeing 62.7 percent of the offensive snaps, but the offense as a whole was broken after Drake Maye went out with an ankle injury early in the first quarter. The offense bogged down with Tommy DeVito at the controls, and Raridon's one target was his fewest in a game since Week 2. Raridon also has been held to single-digit receiving yards in two of the last three contests. He's averaging a robust 13.6 yards per catch this season but isn't a reliable fantasy option with Hunter Henry healthy.

players.comment: Wetjen (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Eagles. Wetjen has operated as the Steelers' top returner on both kickoffs and punts this season. However, with Roman Wilson back from injured reserve and Max Hurleman elevated from the practice squad to the active roster, Wetjen will be a healthy scratch Sunday for the first time this season. Wetjen's next opportunity to play is Friday against the Broncos, although the rookie fourth-rounder's chances of suiting up for that contest would be further diminished if Michael Pittman (foot) is activated from IR before that game.

Daniels caught one of two targets for 22 yards in Sunday's 34-6 win over the Cardinals. With Puka Nacua (knee/toe) and Davante Adams (hamstring) inactive, Daniels' 46 snaps were two fewer than Konata Mumpfield for the team lead at receiver for the Rams. Mumpfield led the group in targets (four), catches (three) and yards (81), and only Xavier Smith (2-40-1) joined him as wide receivers to catch more than one pass from Matthew Stafford against Arizona while the Rams relied heavily on their tight ends and running backs. Daniels' playing time isn't worth chasing in fantasy.

Tate (shoulder) is listed as active for Sunday's game against the Cowboys. Tate, who hasn't played since Week 7, had been listed as questionable for the contest despite being a full practice participant Friday. Now that he's back after missing Tennessee's last two games, the No. 4 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft should immediately reclaim a prominent role in the team's offense in a plus matchup, in the absence of any setbacks or limitations. Tate's return to the lineup arrives at an especially opportune time, given fellow WR Wan'Dale Robinson is out for the season after hurting his ankle last weekend. Prior to sustaining his shoulder injury, Tate had made his mark from a fantasy perspective by catching 34 passes on 51 targets for a team-high 413 yards, to go along with a TD through seven games.

With Tyrell Shavers (knee) cleared to play for Sunday's divisional clash with Miami after spending time on injured reserve, Bell's services won't be needed. His next opportunity to play will come in Week 12 against the Chiefs.

Cisse (ribs) practiced Saturday, Bill Huber of SI.com reports. Cisse was forced out of last Sunday's loss to the Vikings, but his injury isn't considered serious, and it sounds like the cornerback will be ready to go for Wednesday's game against the Rams.

Klein secured all four targets for 24 yards and a touchdown in the Texans' 26-3 win over the Colts on Thursday. Klein surprisingly outpaced veteran position mates Dalton Schultz and Foster Moreau on the night, and the rookie second-round pick, whose only other career reception coming in was a 16-yard grab in Week 1, added his first career touchdown on a 13-yard catch in the third quarter. Given Klein had been a complete non-factor coming into the night, it's difficult to predict whether Thursday's production will have any carryover to a Week 12 home matchup against the Ravens on Sunday, Nov. 29.

Hill (neck) is active for Sunday's game against Dallas. Hill didn't play in Week 10 against the Jaguars, marking his first absence of the 2026 campaign. He logged a full practice Friday but still couldn't avoid a questionable designation. However, the rookie is cleared to suit up in Week 11 for the meeting with the Cowboys, potentially resulting in fewer snaps for Dorian Mausi.

Bernard failed to reel in any of his three targets while notching a 10-yard rush during Sunday night's 38-18 loss to the Bengals. Bernard went without a catch for the first time since Week 1, and his three targets were his fewest since the team's Week 4 loss to the Browns. The wide receiver led his position in offensive snaps (58), besting DK Metcalf (50) in that regard. Bernard entered Week 10 having recorded multiple receptions in five straight contests, and he'll have a good shot to get back on track in Week 11 versus the Eagles.

Coleman carried the ball 17 times for 57 yards and a touchdown and caught all four of his targets for 31 yards in Sunday's 26-21 win over the Panthers. The rookie has seized control of the lead-back role for the Broncos, with his 21 touches dwarfing J.K. Dobbins' five, and Coleman's nine-yard TD run early in the fourth quarter put his team in the lead for good. Coleman has piled up 261 scrimmage yards and two rushing touchdowns over the last three games, and there's no reason to think his role will shrink on the other side of a Week 10 bye.

Trotter recorded eight tackles (five solo) during the Buccaneers' 27-24 loss to the Bears in Week 9. Trotter led the Buccaneers in tackles in Week 9, when he played 59 of 61 defensive snaps (96.7 percent). The rookie second-rounder has logged at least six stops in each of the first eight games of the regular season, and he enters the Week 10 bye with 76 tackles (37 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and three pass defenses (including a pick-six).

Reese logged 13 tackles (four solo) in the Giants' 24-21 loss to the Commanders on Thursday. Reese led the Giants in tackles as a consistent force against the Commanders' run game in the NFC East showdown. Despite the rookie first-rounder's best efforts, the Giants allowed 24 points en route to a meaningful divisional loss.

Klare went without a target while playing four of the Rams' 76 offensive snaps in Sunday's 34-6 win over the Cardinals. Klare has been a healthy inactive on three occasions this season, but he's now suited up in three straight games while the Rams have been short on pass-catching options due to injuries to tight end Terrance Ferguson (hamstring/ankle) and wideouts Puka Nacua (knee), Davante Adams (hamstring) and Jordan Whittington (back). Despite those personnel losses, Klare has still struggled to carve out meaningful playing time, as fellow tight ends Tyler Higbee, Colby Parkinson and Davis Allen are all regarded as superior blockers and have been prioritized ahead of him. The rookie second-round pick out of Ohio State still has yet to draw a target through his first seven NFL games.

Price posted nine carries for 36 yards and one touchdown and gathered in his only target for eight yards during Sunday's 21-13 victory at Las Vegas. This marks Price's fewest touches in a game since returning from IR in Week 8, and he actually was doubled up in the category by position mate Zach Charbonnet, who turned his 20 rushes into 94 yards. Having said that, Price salvaged his day with a 12-yard TD, the first of his career, on the ground in the third quarter. The breakdown of work between the two may signal what's to come in the Seahawks backfield after the team's Week 11 bye, with Price and company set to face off with the NFC West-leading 49ers on the road on Sunday, Nov. 29.

Boettcher recorded six tackles (three solo) during the Colts' 26-3 loss to the Texans on Thursday. Boettcher finished Thursday's game tied for the fourth-most tackles on the Colts. The rookie fourth-rounder has started in each of Indianapolis' last three games, which has lined up with the absence of Akeem Davis-Gaither (knee, IR). Boettcher is up to 50 tackles (16 solo) through 11 regular-season games.

Rodriguez recorded one solo tackle during Sunday's 24-22 loss to the Colts. Rodriguez finished with fewer than eight takedowns for just the third time this season, and his one tackle was a season low for the rookie. The linebacker has now compiled 80 total tackles (36 solo), including a 1.0 sacks, while also adding an interception and a forced fumble over nine contests so far during his rookie campaign.

Douglas (shoulder) will play Sunday against the Bills, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports. Douglas was managed during the practice week, but he's good to go for his normal every-down role Sunday against Buffalo. With the Dolphins installed as 16.5-point underdogs, Miami is projected to throw a ton in comeback mode. However, Douglas is a tough click for fantasy with Kyle McCord under center.

Bell (chest) has returned to Sunday's Week 11 matchup against the Bills, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports. Bell suffered a chest injury late in the first half and was subsequently deemed questionable to return. However, the rookie wideout got back into the game shortly after halftime. Bell will look to be more productive after finishing the first half without a reception.

Taaffe recorded six total tackles (four solo) and an interception during Sunday's 24-22 loss to the Colts. Taaffe was able to register at least six stops for the third straight game and sixth time overall this season. The safety's biggest moment of the game came in the second quarter, when he jumped in front of a short pass from Colts quarterback Daniel Jones, securing his third interception of the year. On the year, Taaffe has compiled 53 total tackles (27 solo), three interceptions and a forced fumble over nine contests so far.

Coleman logged one catch for six yards on six targets in Sunday's Week 10 loss to Indianapolis. Coleman couldn't get on the same page as QB Kyle McCord, who made his first NFL regular-season appearance. In fact, Coleman has been quiet inefficient regardless of who has thrown him the ball this year, as he has just nine receptions on 27 targets through nine games. Two of his nine catches have been touchdowns, but he's not getting enough touches to be a trustworthy fantasy option.

Johnson recorded four total tackles (three solo) and a pick-six in Sunday's 24-22 loss to the Colts. Johnson was able to secure an interception for the second straight week, jumping in front of a pass from Colts quarterback Daniel Jones in the third quarter, ultimately returning the interception for a 59-yard touchdown. The cornerback has now registered 46 total tackles (24 solo), four passes defensed and a forced fumble over nine games this season.

Woods (neck) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Cardinals. Woods opened Week 11 prep with back-to-back full practices before having his reps limited Friday, which prompted the Chiefs to tag him as questionable. The rookie first-rounder has not been cleared by medical staff to play Sunday, so he will miss his third consecutive game due to a neck injury. Bryson Eason and Marcus Harris will continue to operate in rotational roles on the interior defensive line behind Chris Jones and Khyiris Tonga in the absence of Woods, whose next chance to play is Thanksgiving Day against the Bills.

Concepcion caught three of eight targets for 21 yards in Sunday's 27-24 win over Houston. He also gained six yards on one carry. Concepcion finished second on the Browns in targets behind tight end Harold Fannin, who had nine. However, whereas Fannin was able to turn his looks into seven receptions and 91 yards, Concepcion posted a much more modest 3-21-0 line. The rookie wideout departed to the medical tent during the first half of the game due to an undisclosed issue, but he was able to quickly return. Concepcion hasn't put up prolific numbers this season, but he does have at least three receptions in eight of his 10 appearances. Cleveland is on bye in Week 11, so Concepcion will next suit up Sunday, Nov. 29, against Las Vegas.

Thompson (hamstring) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Jets. Thompson's inactive status doesn't come as much of a surprise, given that he entered the weekend as doubtful due to a hamstring injury. He hasn't played since Week 2 against the Raiders, and his next chance to see the field is Week 12 against the Patriots on Nov. 29.

Roush caught both of his two targets for 23 yards during Sunday's 27-24 win versus the Buccaneers. Roush, who has been utilized heavily as a blocker through nine games, achieved a new career high in receiving yards in Week 9. Roush has been relatively efficient with his limited targets so far this season, but Colston Loveland should be expected to continue to handle a substantial majority of the Bears' pass-catching duties at tight end as long as he's available.

Beck (back) has been ruled out for Sunday's game at Kansas City, Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site reports. The Cardinals were already preparing for Josh Johnson to operate as the starting quarterback Sunday, as Beck entered the weekend with the questionable tag due to back spasms. Joey Aguilar will operate as Johnson's backup, and Beck's next opportunity to play is Week 12 against the Commanders on Sunday, Nov. 29.

Mendoza completed 17 of 29 passes for 143 yards, no touchdowns and no interceptions and rushed six times for 22 yards and one TD during Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Seahawks. The Mendoza era in Las Vegas officially kicked off this week following the trade of veteran QB Kirk Cousins to the Vikings, and the rookie first overall pick unsurprisingly flashed at times while also stalling numerous drives by taking six sacks overall. On a positive note, Mendoza didn't turn the ball over, and he also recorded his first touchdown as a pro on a 10-yard run on the Raiders' opening offensive possession. He'll seek to build on the initial start of his career next Sunday at Denver.

Van Roten (hamstring) is active for Sunday's game against the Lions in Munich. Van Roten will be available to make his season debut after spending the first nine weeks of the campaign on injured reserve due to the hamstring issue. He was able to practice throughout Week 10 prep, turning in a pair of a limited sessions Wednesday and Thursday before upgrading to full activity Friday, and the Patriots activated him Saturday. With Ben Brown (knee) and Walter Rouse (concussion) inactive for the Germany game, Van Roten will likely draw the start at left guard.

Moses (knee) has returned to Sunday's game against the Lions in Munich, Mike Reiss of ESPN.com reports. Moses went to the locker room in the first quarter to have his knee injury evaluated. He's been cleared by medical staff to return and is back in at right tackle, with backup Caleb Lomu now on the sidelines.

Patrick (concussion) is questionable for Monday's game against the Bengals. Patrick was a full participant in all three practices during Week 11 prep. Head coach Dan Quinn confirmed with reporters Saturday that Patrick cleared the league's concussion protocol and would start at center Monday, but the injury designation means that is not a guarantee. Nick Allegretti would likely start at center in the event that Patrick doesn't play.

Brown (back) has returned to Thursday's game versus the Colts, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports. Brown left Thursday's contest after suffering a back injury, but he was able to check back in with the Texans' field goal team in the second quarter. With that said, veteran Braden Smith was still working as Houston's right tackle when the first half of Thursday's game ended.

Teller (back) is inactive for Thursday's game versus the Colts. Teller was unavailable in Week 10 against the Browns due to an illness, and he'll be sidelined in Week 11 by a back injury. In his absence, rookie fourth-rounder Febechi Nwaiwu projects as the Texans' top option off the bench at guard.

Tunsil (triceps) is progressing well in his recovery but is not expected to return by the end of the 2026 regular season, Tashan Reed of The Washington Post reports. Tunsil underwent surgery in August to repair a torn triceps. The left tackle continues to recover, but he likely will not suit up for the Commanders in 2026 unless the team makes a playoff run. Even then, it remains unclear whether Tunsil would be able to return at all before the 2027 season.

Shelton (hamstring) is set to miss several weeks due to injury, Greg Beacham of the Associated Press reports. The starting center is set to miss 4-6 weeks with a hamstring injury.
